column2: #939 structural refactor two-axis review (Standards + Correctness/Spec, fresh sessions): P0=0/P1=0/P2=0; 5 P3 + 3 P4 findings, all independently re-verified by the executor (never accepted self-reported). 5 fixed in 99293b7e, 1 fixed in 11ba452f (M-27 `types.py` authoritative comment still said `name` was always defaulted), 2 registered as residuals (`_OBJECT_MODE` duplicated across local_artifact/readonly_fs; broad `attachments.types` re-export face kept deliberately so #938's snapshot guard on origin/main stays green). Guard tests mutation-tested: adding a backend field reddens test_attachment_ref_contract.py, re-adding a dead root re-export reddens test_export_surface.py.

#939 review disposition (comment-only except one assert swap): fixed comments/pointers naming the pre-M-15 home (`attachments.types`) and pre-M-13 home (`local_artifact.py`), the falsified `name` JSDoc in web/src/lib/attachmentRefs.ts, and replaced a tautological `FieldInfo.metadata is not None` assert with a source-level direction assert (independently confirmed by a fresh re-review session: the old one is always true because pydantic v2 metadata is `[]`, the new one reddens when config.py imports the `.types` variant; comment-stripped .ts content byte-identical to e90d025b).

#939 M-27 follow-up: the authoritative `name` docstring in src/agent_harness/attachments/types.py still asserted it was always defaulted, contradicting the pointer the disposition commit had just added to it; 98f28b2b never touched that file despite its message. Comment-only.

#939 Correctness/Spec follow-up: the axis found a SECOND unguarded cross-end mirror of the persisted ref (`tui/src/adapter.ts::TurnImageRef`) whose comment still said the display name was always defaulted, while projection.py and the web contract test both claimed their copy was the only one; corrected both claims and the TUI comment, unified the web construction-site comment with M-27's framing, recorded the missing TUI guard as a residual (same class as the `_OBJECT_MODE` duplication both axes reported).
